signals.signal: The Euronet Collaboration Agreements include a 'Master Services Agreement for ATMs and Recyclers' under which Euronet Card Services is to be the EXCLUSIVE provider of ATM-related technical services to CrediaBank and its affiliates in Greece, conditional on successful transfer/migration of the ATMs to the Euronet network and completion of IT integration. Parallel exclusivity covers merchant acquiring (Euronet MSPI/epay) and card management & issuing processing. Long-stop date for completion is nine months from signing, i.e. 30/09/2026, extendable by mutual agreement; card services full integration is expected from October 2026.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank Company Information Memorandum dated 30/03/2026 — 'Material Contracts — Euronet Agreement' and 'Digital Channels'
signals.implies: A contractual lockout for third-party ATM AND recycler technical services at CrediaBank Greece. Printec's remaining route into this bank's self-service estate is as a sub-supplier to Euronet Card Services, not direct.
signals.likelihood: Binding on completion; completion targeted Q3-2026
signals.followup: Establish whether the recycler exclusivity covers in-branch TCRs bought for the New Experience refits or only ATM-class devices; if it does, pivot the relationship to Euronet Card Services Greece.

signals.signal: Definitive agreement signed 30/12/2025: transfer of the merchant acquiring business to Euronet Merchant Services Payment Institution (epay); transfer of the entire ATM network, on-site and off-site, to Euronet Card Services including its management and operation on the Bank's behalf; free customer access to Euronet's ~2,500-ATM national network; a long-term card management and issuing transaction processing agreement; and an exclusive 3-year eWallet collaboration integrating the IRIS instant-payment rails. Euronet's own release (07/01/2026) puts the combined Greek acquiring operation at more than USD 22bn processed annually and more than 240,000 merchants, closing expected Q3-2026.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank announcement 30/12/2025; Euronet Worldwide press release 07/01/2026
signals.implies: CrediaBank fully exits ATM ownership and card acceptance in Greece. Consolidates Euronet/epay as the dominant Greek acquiring and off-site ATM counterparty — a competitor-positioning signal as much as a lost account.
signals.likelihood: Pending regulatory approval as of Euronet's Q2-2026 call
signals.followup: Re-point Greek ATM/POS/managed-services coverage from CrediaBank to Euronet Card Services and epay; compare against the Piraeus off-site ATM precedent where Printec's Cashflex took the estate.

signals.signal: ATM estate at 31/12/2025: 141 ATMs across Greece, 80 at branch locations and 61 at third-party (off-site) locations — all destined for Euronet Card Services. A live pull of CrediaBank's own branch/ATM locator on 27/08/2026 returns 120 mapped locations: 64 branch sites and 56 off-site ATM locations, i.e. the off-site count is down 5 sites versus the 61 disclosed at 31/12/2025.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank Company Information Memorandum 30/03/2026 ('ATMs'); CrediaBank branch/ATM locator (embedded JSON, machine-readable)
signals.implies: Off-site ATM footprint is being trimmed ahead of the Euronet migration — consistent with a hand-over rather than an expansion. No CrediaBank-side ATM refresh cycle to sell into.
signals.followup: Re-pull the locator after the Euronet completion to measure how many CrediaBank-branded off-site sites survive under Euronet operation.

signals.signal: H1-2026 branch transformation: 24 branches targeted for rebranding to the 'New Experience' model by end-2026 — 8 completed to date, 6 scheduled by early Q4-2026, remaining 10 on track for delivery by year-end. Network flat at 66 branches (H1-2025: 66); FTEs 1,223, down 3% YoY after a voluntary exit scheme. Recurring opex of EUR 76.7m, up 4% YoY, is explicitly attributed to the digital transformation and the branch renovations programme (plus EUR 3m of Malta preparation costs).
signals.source_name: CrediaBank H1 2026 Financial Results Presentation, slides 20 and 25
signals.implies: 16 branch refits still to be delivered inside ~5 months, each carrying a cash-automation and self-service fit-out. This is the live, funded, dated opportunity at this bank.
signals.followup: Identify the branch fit-out integrator and the incumbent TCR/VTS hardware brand at the completed 8 sites before the next 16 are specified.

signals.signal: The 'New Experience' branch specification is explicitly cash-automation-led: customers are identified via their bank card on entry; cash transactions are completed through TCR (teller cash recycler) machines; open transaction and collaboration areas replace the conventional teller counter; VTS (virtual teller stations) run the CrediaConnect remote-service product; plus an interactive product-exploration system developed with FORTH. Confirmed in the Thessaloniki opening at 8 Tsimiski Street (04/02/2026) and the Panepistimiou/Omirou opening (06/05/2026), after first launches in Heraklion and Athens/Skoufa in December 2025.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank press releases: 'CrediaBank has opened its first New Experience branch in Thessaloniki' (04/02/2026) and 'Opening of the New Experience Branch on Panepistimiou Street' (06/05/2026)
signals.implies: Direct fit for Printec cash automation / recyclers and self-service / virtual-teller. A counterless branch needs a TCR at every serving position, not one machine per site.
signals.followup: Confirm the recycler brand installed at Tsimiski 8 and Panepistimiou, and whether VTS hardware is separately sourced from the TCRs.

signals.signal: CEO Eleni Vrettou at the Panepistimiou opening (06/05/2026): the goal is 'renewing 40% of the network by the end of 2026'. The March-2026 CIM goes further: 'Over the next two years, the Group plans to gradually remodel its entire branch network into New Experience branches. Features will include personalized recognition, teller cash recyclers and enhanced accessibility for individuals with special needs. In flagship branches, the customer experience will be further elevated through the integration of cutting-edge technologies such as interactive screens and virtual teller stations.' Branch mix at 31/12/2025: Attica 22, Crete 17, Northern Greece 18, Peloponnese 4, other 5 — total 66.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank press release 06/05/2026; CrediaBank Company Information Memorandum 30/03/2026, 'Branches'
signals.implies: A stated intent to fit TCRs across all 66 branches by roughly 2028 — a repeatable multi-year cash-automation pipeline of ~42 sites beyond the 24 committed for 2026.
signals.followup: Pitch a phased TCR plus virtual-teller rollout for the post-2026 tranche while the 2026 tranche is still being specified.

signals.signal: Digital Transformation Program (launched October 2025): the Group plans to invest more than EUR 60.0 million over 2026-2028 and has assembled a dedicated technology team of more than 80 experienced professionals. Scope explicitly covers a digitization strategy for both Greece and Malta, expansion of branch-network rebranding, end-to-end digital workflow optimisation, modernization of core banking systems, strengthening of regulatory, compliance, cybersecurity and risk management frameworks, a digital performance and governance model, and a unified CRM. Core banking is Temenos T24 (R17) with a Payments HUB (R17/R23); infrastructure is already outsourced to a managed service partner on Sparkle DC.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank Company Information Memorandum 30/03/2026, 'Digital Transformation Program in Motion' and 'Digital Channels — Digital Transformation Program'
signals.implies: A named, budgeted three-year programme with explicit AML/compliance, risk, cyber and core-modernisation line items. The bank already outsources infrastructure, so managed services is a proven buying pattern here.
signals.followup: Target the compliance/risk-systems, transaction-monitoring and HSM/security workstreams — these sit outside the Euronet exclusivity, which is confined to acquiring, card processing and ATM/recycler technical services.

signals.signal: Dated H1-2026 digital delivery milestones: Customer Care go-live (September 2026), Friends & Family release of the new digital experience (September 2026), Digital Instant Loan (October 2026), omnichannel rollout (November 2026). Q2-2026 already moved from build-up to production: CRM/Customer 360, personalized data-driven campaigns and lending automation are live on Azure and cloud data foundations. Digital channel penetration exceeded 70% of the active customer base at 31/12/2025 with a 56% activity rate among registered users; digital transaction value reached ~EUR 6.0bn in 2025.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank H1 2026 Financial Results Presentation, slide 26; CIM 30/03/2026 for the 2025 penetration figures
signals.implies: A fully digital instant-loan journey going live in October 2026 requires remote identity verification at scale — a concrete digital onboarding / eKYC entry point with a hard date.
signals.followup: Approach on eKYC / remote identification and document verification before the October-2026 Digital Instant Loan go-live locks a vendor in.

signals.signal: Expected closing of the 70.03% HSBC Bank Malta acquisition has moved to Q2 2027 — the September-2025 announcement and subsequent coverage had indicated end-2026. HSBC Malta CEO stated on the record on 05/08/2026 that the takeover awaits regulatory approval (MFSA, Bank of Greece, ECB) and would then close in Q2 2027. HSBC Malta H1-2026 stand-alone: recurring PBT EUR 51.7m (vs EUR 58.7m H1-2025), net loans EUR 2.7bn, customer deposits EUR 6.2bn, loan-to-deposit 43%, CET1 24.7%, total capital 27.8%, NPE 2.3%; estimated badwill c. EUR 238m on the fixed EUR 200m price. Pantelakis Securities (70%) and Evropi Holdings both expected to close Q4 2026; the three transactions are guided to add c. EUR 45m EBT by 2028.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank H1 2026 Financial Results Presentation, slides 7 and 9; The Malta Independent, 'CrediaBank-HSBC takeover expected to close in Q2 2027, HSBC Malta CEO says' (05/08/2026)
signals.implies: Malta separation and integration spend now falls in 2027, not 2026 — an 18-month runway to position for the carve-out of a full retail bank off HSBC group platforms (core, cards, AML/sanctions screening, monitoring, HSM, managed services).
signals.followup: Build a Malta separation/integration proposition now for a 2027 decision window; Malta is outside the Euronet Greek exclusivity.

signals.signal: HSBC Malta operated 12 branches (11 in Malta, 1 in Gozo) and 63 ATMs at 31/12/2025, serving ~161,000 retail customers with ~923 average employees. It REPLACED ITS ENTIRE ATM FLEET during 2025 — new machines with touchscreen capability, multi-check deposit and CRPD-compliant accessibility (signage, lighting, height/layout) — which, with the Qormi head-office refurbishment, drove group depreciation and impairment of PPE up 50.5% from EUR 3.2m to EUR 4.9m. 95% of retail transactions ran through online channels in 2025; SEPA Instant Payments launched in 2025.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank Company Information Memorandum 30/03/2026, HSBC Malta Group business description and MD&A
signals.implies: No ATM hardware refresh opportunity in Malta for years. The Malta opening is managed services, monitoring and AML/compliance around a newly installed estate that will lose its HSBC group support arrangements at carve-out.
signals.followup: Identify the vendor and service contract behind the 2025 HSBC Malta ATM replacement — a group frame agreement is unlikely to survive the sale, creating a service-transition opening at Q2-2027.

signals.signal: Open vacancies listed on CrediaBank's own careers page as at 27/08/2026 include Head of KYC Operations, IT Security Expert, Chief Architect, Payments Operations Expert, IT Auditor, IT Business Analyst and Data & Reporting Engineer — consistent with the CIM's stated 80+ person technology team and the compliance/cyber workstream of the Digital Transformation Program. Caveat: the vacancies index page carries a stale 'Published on: 06 November, 2025' stamp, so individual posting dates are not verifiable from this page.
signals.implies: Hiring pattern corroborates in-flight KYC-operations, security and architecture build-out — the buying centres for eKYC, AML/compliance and HSM/security sit inside functions currently being staffed.
signals.followup: Map the Head of KYC Operations and IT Security Expert hires once filled; they are the likely evaluators for onboarding and security tooling.

coverage_notes: Fresh run, no checkpoint existed. Primary-source-first: the H1-2026 results presentation (06/08/2026), the Company Information Memorandum dated 30/03/2026 (~1.4m characters, by far the richest disclosure on this bank and not used by the previous run), the 30/12/2025 Euronet announcement PDF, two New Experience branch press-release PDFs, the 09/03/2026 Capital Markets Day announcement, Euronet Worldwide's own IR release (07/01/2026), and a live machine-readable pull of the bank's branch/ATM locator on 27/08/2026. Searched in both English and Greek across the bank's IR and press office, Euronet IR, Greek financial press (mononews, capital, insider, reporter, imerisia, iefimerida, dealnews, powergame, topontiki, crisismonitor) and Maltese press (Malta Independent, MaltaToday, Newsbook, whoswho.mt), plus law-firm deal announcements (Milbank). Four angles were varied deliberately versus the usual route: (1) the securities-offering disclosure document rather than the results deck, which is where the Euronet contract-level exclusivity and the EUR 60m IT budget actually live; (2) the branch-locator JSON embedded in the public site, giving an independent 27/08/2026 count; (3) the acquirer-side counterparty (Euronet IR) rather than only the bank; (4) the Maltese-press angle on the target, which is where the Q2-2027 slip was said on the record first. Genuine gaps: no Greek Competition Commission (Epitropi Antagonismou) decision on the Euronet concentration was locatable, so clearance status is unconfirmed; the vendor behind the installed TCR/VTS units in the New Experience branches is not disclosed anywhere public and remains the single most valuable unknown for Printec; the vendor of HSBC Malta's 2025 full ATM replacement is likewise undisclosed; and CrediaBank publishes no procurement register (it is a private-sector bank, so Diavgeia/ESIDIS do not apply). All confidence capped at Medium per the rules, with the careers-page row at Low because its index date is stale.
